title: Implement durable projection outbox and projection repair

projection_contract.canonical_authority: memory_records and lifecycle/event-journal rows remain canonical inside the single sovereign_state::StateStore SQLite authority
projection_contract.outbox_semantics: refresh intent only; replay always rereads the current canonical memory row and never treats queued payload as truth
projection_contract.one_pending_repair_per_projection_kind: partial UNIQUE index memory_projection_repairs_one_pending_idx enforces at most one pending repair for memory_fts_v1
projection_contract.migration_bootstrap: v5->v6 clears disposable FTS rows and seeds one coalesced memory_fts_v1 outbox intent for every canonical memory row
projection_contract.migration_failure_semantics: v6 DDL/data changes are transactional; a deliberately failing v6 fixture leaves the v5 database/version intact and an exact v5 backup remains readable/upgradeable

transaction_boundaries.canonical_txn_a: canonical lifecycle mutation + append-only lifecycle journal + SQLite-triggered outbox enqueue/coalesce commit together before projection delivery
transaction_boundaries.projection_txn_b: bounded replay rereads the CURRENT canonical row, deletes all FTS rows for that memory_id, inserts the exact canonical projection row, and deletes the matching outbox intent in one transaction
transaction_boundaries.post_commit_failure: projection delivery failure is returned as MemoryError::ProjectionPending so a caller cannot infer that already-committed canonical truth rolled back
transaction_boundaries.missing_canonical: an outbox reference whose canonical row is absent is treated as integrity corruption; replay fails closed and does not consume the durable intent
transaction_boundaries.duplicate_delivery: DELETE-all + INSERT-from-current-canonical + same-transaction outbox deletion converges idempotently even after repeated/coalesced delivery

startup_and_repair.startup: resume any durable pending repair first, then drain pending outbox refreshes; startup does not perform an unconditional whole-corpus consistency scan
startup_and_repair.pending_repair_retry: repair_projection completes an already-pending repair before considering a new R1 record, so an R1-committed/R2-failed same-process retry cannot collide with the one-pending invariant
startup_and_repair.explicit_consistency_repair: repair_projection performs an explicit integrity-suspicion consistency check and creates a durable pending repair only when canonical/projection rows disagree
startup_and_repair.repair_r1: pending ProjectionRepair record commits durably before rebuild
startup_and_repair.repair_r2: full derived FTS rebuild from canonical memory + covered outbox clear + exact repair transition to completed commit atomically

crash_and_corruption_proof.crash_after_canonical_before_projection: integration-test child removes only the disposable derived FTS table to force post-canonical projection delivery failure through the production MemoryManager path; capture returns ProjectionPending after canonical/outbox commit, test-only child then aborts, and parent proves canonical row + outbox survive before recreating the derived table and reopening for startup replay
crash_and_corruption_proof.missing_canonical_corruption_fixture: a separate test connection disables foreign_keys only to manufacture an impossible/corrupt outbox reference; normal StateStore connections retain foreign_keys=ON and replay fails closed while retaining that intent
crash_and_corruption_proof.damaged_projection_rebuild: missing, mismatched, and orphan FTS rows are detected by explicit repair_projection and rebuilt solely from canonical memory

retrieval_compatibility.synchronous_search_visibility: normal lifecycle APIs synchronously drain the durable outbox after canonical commit when projection service is healthy
retrieval_compatibility.v4_to_current_searchability: legacy v4 memory migrates through v5/v6, startup outbox replay rebuilds FTS, and retrieval remains searchable

resource_ownership.nuance: M4-T03 does not claim that StateStore connection defaults prove architecture-wide aggregate SQLite cache/mmap/WAL-health hard limits; broader process resource enforcement remains separately owned.

verification.detail: 8/8 projection integration tests; 2/2 projection-named retrieval regressions
lifecycle 25/25; projection 8/8; retrieval 18/18; doc tests pass
all workspace tests passed; only intentional local-model qualification/smoke tests ignored

initial_blockers: test crash environment variable could abort ordinary production builds
missing canonical row during outbox delivery was silently consumed
repair retry did not reuse a durable pending repair
startup performed an unconditional full consistency scan with poor FTS lookup scaling
repairs: removed production crash/abort seam; forced crash now exists only in integration-test child code after the production API reports post-commit ProjectionPending
missing canonical outbox references now fail closed and retain reconciliation evidence
repair_projection resumes an existing pending repair before creating any new repair
startup is bounded to pending-repair resume + outbox drain; whole-projection integrity scan/rebuild is explicit
independent_audit.notes: Fresh exact-tree read-only re-audit confirmed all four blockers repaired, v6 schema/outbox/repair semantics coherent, focused tests and strict quality gates green, and no second DB/fallback/vector authority introduced.
